body:
Two independent gaps in `cps/api/edit.py:set_cover`:

1. No `helper.book_cover_is_locked` check. `cover_picker.cover_picker_apply` refuses every
   apply kind with a 409 while the per-book cover lock is set (janeczku/calibre-web#2165), and
   the classic editor honours it on its cover-URL path. The SPA endpoint writes regardless, so a
   user who deliberately locked a cover can have it replaced from the new UI's edit page.
2. It resolves the book with `calibre_db.get_filtered_book(book_id)` using strict defaults,
   while `cps/api/books.py`'s detail endpoint deliberately passes
   `allow_show_archived=True, allow_show_hidden=True` so a user can open their OWN hidden or
   archived book. The neighbouring delete endpoints in the same module pass those flags too.
   Result: the edit page opens, and replacing the cover 404s.

Found by an adversarial review of PR #1739. Not fixed there: both are behaviour changes
unrelated to that PR's cache policy, and (1) in particular would newly refuse writes that
currently succeed, which deserves its own change and its own release note.
title: SPA cover endpoint ignores the cover lock and 404s on the user's own hidden or archived book

resolution.note: Both gaps fixed in cps/api/edit.py::set_cover. (1) The book is resolved with allow_show_archived=True, allow_show_hidden=True, matching delete_book (:409) and delete_format (:428) in the same module - both WRITE endpoints, so the precedent transfers directly. Those two flags gate per-user state (ub.ArchivedBook and ub.UserHiddenBook filter on user_id), so the relaxation reaches a book the caller personally hid or archived and is otherwise authorized to see; language, allowed/denied tags, the custom-column ACL and the personal-library membership predicate all still apply, and allow_show_global is deliberately NOT passed. (2) The per-book cover lock is consulted before any write and refused with 409, matching cover_picker_apply in status and meaning (the JSON envelopes differ per endpoint convention). Checking visibility BEFORE the lock is also the right information-disclosure order: a book the caller may not see 404s without revealing its lock state. LIMIT OF THE GUARANTEE, stated rather than implied: helper.book_cover_is_locked returns False on ANY exception, so a failing lock query silently permits the overwrite - filed as F-33dea0, not changed here. A check-to-write race also remains (pre-existing, shared with the picker; every editor can unlock anyway, so it is not a security boundary). TESTS, precisely: 4 tests in test_f65c93f_spa_set_cover_policy.py, all red on the parent. Three are source assertions; the fourth touches the module object and catches the wrong-namespace bug in isolation - VERIFIED by running that test alone against that mutant. The pre-existing executing tests in test_api_v1_edit.py catch it too, so that coverage is redundant, not absent. Mutation-tested 5 ways, all red.
